New Horison Admin

By: Sophia Phirippides | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
No horizons for ex-miners who have had their retrenchment payments taken off them by a financial company claiming they can get them more. We confront New Horizon on their theft of ex-miners’ pension

Unique Selling Point:
No Horizons – New Horison Stealing Pensions... Getting retrenched is devastating, but many are consoled by the opportunity that comes with receiving their severance package. It’s a chance to build that dream house, to pay for children and grandchildren to go to university, or to tend to medical needs for the foreseeable future. But that dream was shattered for a group of Anglo Ashanti Miners in Fochville by a company based in Vanderbijlpark, called New Horizon Administration, who has targeted ex-miners retrenchment funds for fraud. Now, most of them are facing an uncertain future.

Summary:
In 2017 a group of miners took voluntary retrenchment packages offered by Anglo Ashanti Gold In Carltonville. The miners were then approached by a company based in Vanderbijlpark called New Horizon Administration run by the MacPherson family. The owner is Alberta MacPherson, managed by daughter Zenobia MacPherson - she is listed as the active director. which alleged that Anglo Ashanti had short changed the workers and that they were due more- some were promised packages to the tune of 2 Million rands each (depending on years of service), The company promised the miners that they could recover these monies from Anglo Ashanti for them( Including recalculating and getting UIF settlements for them) ... all they needed was a sizeable deposit from each miner-unfortunately many obliged and made deposits to this company. They were told they were going to get their “residual “ payments in 6 to 8 weeks... this never occurred.

Anglo Ashanti has since denied ever having dealings with this company, and has stated all due monies were paid over. The company to date is still stringing the miners along.

Further information:
New Horizon is still operating and continues to scam unsuspecting workers. Alberta MacPherson and her company AM Legal Advisory Service was the subject of an FSB alert in 2014, also for claiming to recover surplus funds for clients which after the customers paid a fee never arrived. We will interview the successor to FSB, Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), concerning their jurisdiction and the continuing operation of Alberta MacPherson when they knew about her unscrupulous dealings as early as 2014.

We will have an opportunity for a potentially explosive confront. Sinethemba spent a week scouting their movement, in most cases Zenobia MacPherson (the Manager) and Alberta MacPherson are usually at the office until about 19:30 PM or 20:00 PM, they are always fetched by what Sinethemba assumea are the husbands. In terms of following them we could only pin Zenobia to one address.

There are at least 20 case studies who were scammed and lost tens of thousands of Rands.
Some of the case studies have since opened cases against the company and Alberta MacPherson.
All our case studies have proof (In terms of financial paper work).
We know that she is still operating.
We have undercover footage obtained over two days. This shows how the company operates and how they sell their services to unsuspecting victims.

Case Studies to be interviewed:

- Zwelinzima Yende - 52 years old Zwelinzima Yende worked as a mine electrician at Anglo Ashanti Gold for 21 years , but in 2017 he was one of the unfortunate workers to be made redundant and was offered a voluntary retrenchment package -which he accepted .In the same year he heard of a company that was willing to assist retrenched workers recover monies that were allegedly owed to them ( the rouse was that Anglo Ashanti Gold had short changed the workers and that they were due far more than they received from the severance package and pension fund.

Zwelinzima approached New Horizon Administration, who offered to assist him. The company alleged that Anglo Ashanti had short changed Zwelinzima by R661 000 for his retrenchment package, and that he was suppose to receive R 2,6 million for his pension fund with sentinel ( instead of the (R700 000 he received).

The company promised that the monies could be recovered in 7- 8 weeks guaranteed, and that the company would charge a 25 percent fee for services rendered. Zwelinzima paid a deposit of R 78 996.69. AZwlfter a few months Zwelinzima realised the money wasn’t forthcoming and that he’d been deceived – he approached the company for answers and was told to be patient,he was then told Anglo Ashanti Gold was about to make payments and that this will happen in due course.In 2019 Zwelinzima still persisted ,but was met with rudeness and indifference by member of the Mcpherson family.

After realising that this was all a scam Zwelinzima sought other mineworkers who had been scammed in the same way and formed an action group – trying to get answers and recover their monies. He opened a case in 2020 after failed attempts to reason with New Horizon, the case was transferred to the Hawks in Germiston, but they did not get much joy from the investigating officers and were told their case was withdrawn ( He never spoke to the investigating officers, further statements were not taken, and no evidence was ever collected from him)

Zwelinzima and the group persisted and tried to go the civil route, but couldn’t afford the legal fees.Zwelinzima feels responsible for the other group members, as some of them lost huge amounts of money. We will have to interview him in vernacular, as his English is limited.


- Lloyd Tsotetsi - 47 year Old Lloyd Tsotetsi worked as a mine fit and turner at Anglo Ashanti Gold for 21 years ,in 2017 he was among workers who were made redundant , he was also offered a voluntary retrenchment package -which he accepted ( He received R470 000), he also got R 700 000 from his pension fund. He was referred to New Horizon by a fellow mine worker. New Horizon stated that he was suppose to get R 1 Million for his pension fund, and that they could recover these monies in just 7 – 8 weeks… He never received any money and has been waiting for year, he has tried to approach the company many times and has also been met with rudeness. He paid the company R 345 000 in total. Currently Llyod says he is suffering from depression and is struggling to get assistance as he doesn’t have much money left. He has 3 children , with the eldest due to go to varsity soon… he states that he will not be able to afford to send his eldest to school next year. Llyod is currently squatting in a mine owned house in Fochville and expects to be evicted at any time. He has also opened a case.

- Itumeleng Tsuduba – 58 year old Itumeleng Tsuduba worked at Anglo Ashanti Gold for 34 years as a shift manager, in 2017 he was retrenched from the mine, he was offered a voluntary retrenchment package – which he accepted (he received R 1 million for his 34 year service), he also received 1,8 Million from his pension fund with Sentinel. He was advised by a mine worker to contact New horizon regarding discrepancies in his pay out, he approached New Horizon who stated that he was actually suppose to receive in excess of R 6 Million in total for both the VSP and pension fund due to his long service at the mine. He was asked to pay a deposit -which he did and handed New Horizon R 654 141.09.Itumeleng has lost all hope of getting his money back, he had hoped to set up a trust fund for his youngest son who is 12. Itumeleng has not opened a case yet and says as much as he has lost hope, a part of him is hoping he will get something back.

- Labour Law Expert Patrick Deale of Deale Attorneys – we had a telephonic meeting with Patrick who dismissed New Horizon as nothing but a scam targeting ill-informed, vulnerable mine workers.

Press Release:


Retrenched mine workers say they’ve been duped out of hundreds of thousands of rands by a company in Vanderbijlpark. Carte Blanche investigates the practices of the company that has allegedly drained money from former mine workers’ retrenchment payouts.

Script:


LINK: Getting retrenched is devastating, but many are consoled with the opportunity that comes with a severance package.
Zweli: I had to settle the car. and then I had to buy the house.

VO: Retrenched in 2017, Zwelibanzi Yende, a mine locomotive electrician, had hopes of getting his life in order.// beat// and Lloyd Tsotetsi worked on the mines as a fitter and turner. He had big plans for his children's education.
Lloyd: I've got 3 children. Firstborn is 18 years, she's supposed to be going to tertiary next year.
LINK: But that dream was shattered for a group of AngloGold Ashanti employees who were told by a consulting company, New Horison admin, that they were short changed and should be getting more.

Lloyd: I felt like I've been underpaid. That is why I ended up going to New Horisons. They said the mines are not paying people what is due to them.


VO: Zwelibanzi Yende was sold a similar story by New Horison Admin.// BEAT//

Formed in 2016, it's a family business run by the McPhersons in Vanderbijlpark, Gauteng. Mom Albertha, resigned as a director in 2017, but still works there. Daughter Zenobia is now the sole director and her sister Juritha handles the front desk.

They claim that New Horison can retrieve extra money for their clients by reassessing and recalculating their voluntary severance packages or VSPs, including pension and provident funds as well as other benefits, such as workplace injury claims, even after they've been settled.

Lloyd: For instance, on VSP, they had their own calculation. They said I've been robbed.

VO: According to Lloyd Tsotetsi, it was Albertha, who in 2017 told him he should have received over a million rand more just on his VSP. He had to pay an upfront deposit of R55 000, and New Horison would take 25% of any additional funds retrieved.

Lloyd: She promised that I'm gonna get it from six to eight weeks.

VO: Zwelibanzi Yende's deposit was almost R79 000. New Horison recalculated his VSP and pension and told him to expect over R2.6 million extra - written on this post-it note.
[beat] As far as they both understood, New Horison's 25% was based on additional funds. But Lloyd was in for a shock after his original pension settlement of around R660 000, came into his bank account.
Lloyd: Then after getting my pension fund, she demanded 288,000.
Derek: Did you pay that?
Lloyd: She was intimidating that she'll send the Sheriff to take everything that I have.
VO: He was confused - Albertha was asking for money, even though the additional 1.7 million rand he was promised on his pension was not yet forthcoming. To date he has paid New Horison over R340 000 rand, and collectively just this group of ex AngloGold Ashanti employees have forked out close to 3 million rand in fees. Four years later, they say no extra money has materialised.

Maria: That lady, she must pay us back. That money doesn't belong to her, it's our money.

VO: The payment of a large deposit, with the promise of substantial rewards, are the hallmarks of what the FBI calls an Advance Fee Scheme.
We sent in an undercover operative to New Horison Admin to investigate, posing as a retrenched mine worker.
She pays R600 for a consultation, and Juritha explains how they get their clients more money.

Juritha: this is how the VSP retrenchment package works, once we get the calculations we get the upfront deposit. The upfront deposit goes with the calculations to the mine, the mine has 6 weeks to accept. If the mine does not accept in the 6 weeks, then our lawyers take over, then they take them to court, forcing them to get a court interdict to order them to pay that money.

VO: So what did Juritha just say? // Freeze on shot// Labour Law expert Patrick Deale considers this sale’s spiel.

Patrick: I think we have a case of fraud on our hands more commonly known as a scam - there's no basis for any of those things. They're trying to sound like big, threatening lawyers and trying to intimidate these institutions, which they have no right to, and there's no prospect of them getting anything out of them.

VO: At reception, Juritha tells our undercover operative that she was short paid, despite the very scant information she was given.

Juritha: So it’s 11 years and you only received under R50000… Basic salary with the 8.3 and 3.7 that you received, just a rough estimation she was at least supposed to get 300,000
VO: Amidst some light hearted banter she is handed a bundle of documents to sign
Juritha: Mama, usigna full signature like you are signing at the bank.

Zweli: "sign here, sign here" you see, we just sign. when I asked why can't you explain or give us these papers. so that I can take them at home to read this thing. "no, no, no, no, look, this paperwork is money, to print all those papers, you see?

VO: Zenobia spins our operative a different story
Zenobia: Unfortunately I do not give copies of my documentation due to the fact that fraud has been committed with it.
VO: Zwelibanzi was allowed to leave with his post-it note - a record of the money he should expect.

Derek: How would New Horison have arrived at these increased amounts?
Patrick: There's no indication about how they came about the formula for these calculations, so they would have to explain where the right comes from and that right could only have come from their pre-existing retrenchment agreements, which, in this case, was facilitated by the CCMA.

VO: After 34 years working his way up to shift boss, Itumeleng Tsuduba was also retrenched from AngloGold Ashanti and received over 2 million rand. He felt he’d got a raw deal.
Itumeleng: Yeah, I was not happy.
VO: His wife Elizabeth, heard about New Horison from a friend.
Elizabeth: I regret that day really, because I'm the one who introduced my husband into this mess.

Derek: Elizabeth, describe that meeting with Alberta. What did she promise?
Elizabeth: She came up with the huge number of money pension fund is how much, retrenchment is how much, the silicosis is going to be how much, all in all, it was 11 million.
Derek: You must have both felt like you'd hit the jackpot.
Elizabeth: Of course yes.

VO: Itumeleng ended up paying New Horison over R650 000.

Derek: And you've never got a cent out of them?
Elizabeth: Nothing. Even a single cent.

Patrick: If you're going to tempt people, don't hang a small sweet in front of them, hang something large, that it's worth investing trust in and to induce them to pay the deposit.

VO: The people who approached Carte Blanche, report that as money from their original payouts came into their bank accounts, uncannily, Albertha or Zenobia would call them demanding the 25% fee, but when they asked for their money in return they were given a slew of excuses.

Zweli: So that six to eight weeks passed. So we keep on phoning them. "No, don't worry, the case is in Supreme Court. No the mine also give us problem they don't want to pay."every time stories, stories, stories.

Lloyd: The last time when we went to them, the lady told us the monies are there, but Tito Mboweni is still talking to Ramaphosa to release money together with Reserve Bank.
Derek: Is this the story they told you?
Lloyd: Ey, big story like ay

Elizabeth: When we go there she just shouting, talking vulgar language, she gonna sue us and she gonna sell our houses.

Patrick: That's part of the threatening, kind of psychology to put fear into them that if they challenge it in any way, they could be in trouble.

VO: And to make matters worse Zwelibanzi Yende received an additional bill for R145 000 rand.

Derek: What do they say that's for?
Zweli: They say for their services. telephone, Follow up.

Patrick: The deposit is there as part payment of a service to be rendered. Those monies have not been received,And on that basis, the individual can cancel the contract and repay, claim repayment of the deposit for the service that has not been rendered.

LINK: A group of the retrenched workers got tired of waiting and laid charges with the police in July last year. But in May they got an SMS saying that the case had been withdrawn and the docket closed

VO: They called WO Pretorius for an explanation on the prosecutor's findings.
Pretorius: They [New Horison Admin]) state they didn’t take anybody’s money, they took a deposit and they took money when the payouts are made into people’s accounts and the people are supposed to pay them.
VO: Dissatisfied with the extent of the police investigation, the miners went back to New Horison and were met by an angry Zenobia.

Sound up: Undercover day 3:
Zenobia: You all know you went to the police station, mos, ne? Yes, now what do you want me to do?
Zweli: I want my money back:
Zenobia: I want my services, my fees for services rendered. I want that
VO: And we bet she does, because according to the documents we glimpsed, their clients actually sign away 25% of any incoming benefits into their bank accounts, from the date of signature, to New Horison. The same documents they never get a copy of.

VO: So the time had come for a face to face with the head honcho.

Cut to Derek knocking on the door and then making the phone call…
Derek: Good morning Zenobia how are you doing? It's Derek Watts from Carte Blanche. I want to speak to you about new horizon and the deposits that you've taken allegedly under false pretenses.
zenobia: Derek, well you have to make an appointment.
Derek: I'm right at your door.
zenobia: I'm not at the office as yet. Send your queries through to me and I'll have my legal team look at it and then we can see from there

VO: First they offered to go through each file in detail, //but three weeks later, they were not prepared to answer to specifics. In their response they implied that it is commonplace for companies and pension funds to “inaccurately calculate employment benefits and compensation”.
Page 5 clause 15: ROR reference
"The service provider has extensive knowledge and experience, that were accumulated over the past thirty years. Employers and/or administrators of the various Funds referred to, inaccurately calculates employment benefits and compensation "

LINK: AngloGold Ashanti say that all of the retrenched workers were paid according to the laws and agreed by the unions. They say that they've never been approached by New Horison or any of their representatives regarding the settlements.

VO: We asked New Horison to show proof of work and which institutions they had contacted, no specific proof was provided. They denied any wrongdoing and said they fulfilled their contracts with their customers.
The unions for the mineworkers NUM and UASA, and pension fund Sentinel, also confirm that they have not received any disputes concerning these matters.
New Horison further denies any allegation that their clients received no money, pointing to our own summary that “substantial amounts were received" and attribute those results to services they rendered. But the amounts we reflected in our summary were from the original AngloGold Ashanti settlements.

Page 8 clause 25: ROR reference
"The allegations that clients have not received a single cent is untrue and it is evident on your own summary that substantial amounts were received by clients respectively. It should be mentioned that the Complainants had received payments of benefits from their previous or former employers. The services the service provider rendered, resulted into payment of the correct calculation of unpaid benefits and of compensation still payable. "
VO: It appears this is how New Horison understands the catch-all clause in their Client Fee Agreement, which claims 25% of all benefits received after the initial R600 consultation.
Page 14 Clause 6: ROR reference
"The Principal/Client shall pay the Service Provider and non-refundable consultation fee of R600.00 at the time of the initial consultation. Thereafter, the Principal/Client shall be liable to the Service Provider for Payment of the Services Provide, the fees to be equal but not to excess of 25% of the amount received. Such benefits shall include any and all payments received in terms of the Principal/Client's Employee Benefits."
VO: They claim that the formula for their recalculations is privileged… and a lengthy and complicated process performed by actuaries.
VO: Our undercover footage suggests otherwise
Juritha: I can send it through now to the forensic auditor so that we can see how much is her VSP outstanding
Undercover: Like now…
Juritha: We gonna get it now
Page 7 clause 21: ROR reference
"Your request to disclose the "formula" of how the service provider calculates the underpaid or unpaid benefits to clients, is privileged."
VO: The miners allege they were given calculations within a day of engaging their services and that recovery of funds would take 6 to 8 weeks. New Horison refutes this as not only untrue, but potentially impossible:
Page 8 clause 25: ROR reference
"The allegations that outstanding monies will be retrieved and/or recovered within a period of six to eight weeks, not only is untrue, but potentially impossible."
[undercover] Juritha: The VSP that one there’s a upfront payment that needs to be paid, and that one takes 6-8 weeks.
Page 5 clause 17: ROR reference
"For purposes of the recalculation and for various types of packages, due to the complex nature of the recalculation, the service provider utilizes the services of Actuaries and legal experts to render the required services to the clients."
VO: They say the ex-miners’ allegations are a smear campaign and that they're the authors of their own misfortune.
Page 2 clause 4: I’m using pg 10 point 26.6
"It is abundantly clear, that the complainants that approached you, have one objection of consideration, is to drive a smearing campaign against our clients."
VO: They also state "as a result of the Complainants actions, the service provider voluntarily terminated their services”, which they say could explain why payments have not been received by clients to date. And instead they claim that money is owed to them.
Counter claim mentioned at Page 1 Clause 3
Page 7 clause 22: ROR reference
"The service provider is not of the intention to engage into any further elaboration of the matters of those complainants that approached you, included in your list. It is however pointed out, that as a result of the Complainants actions, the service provider voluntarily terminated their services, as a result of a breakdown in the trust relationship."


Patrick: These are mine workers. Can you imagine the kind of work that they've done on the mines, they finally been paid out,, and they get tempted to a pot at the end of the rainbow, and they're left destitute.

Derek: So what is your hope for your financial future?
Lloyd: It’s bleek. It’s doom. that pension fund that I work for 21 years is gone.

Elizabeth: My husband now I can see is now no longer my husband because the few money that we did left with, we use it because we know there is huge money that is coming you can think of 11 million when its coming it’s a lot.

from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 22 August 2021 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 10 September 2021 Press Release: Retrenched mine workers say they’ve been duped out of hundreds of thousands of rands by a company in Vanderbijlpark. Carte Blanche investigates the practices of the company that has allegedly drained money from former mine workers’ retrenchment payouts. Script: LINK: Getting retrenched is devastating, but many are consoled with the opportunity that comes with a severance package. Zweli: I had to settle the car. and then I had to buy the house. VO: Retrenched in 2017, Zwelibanzi Yende, a mine locomotive electrician, had hopes of getting his life in order.// beat// and Lloyd Tsotetsi worked on the mines as a fitter and turner. He had big plans for his children's education. Lloyd: I've got 3 children. Firstborn is 18 years, she's supposed to be going to tertiary next year. LINK: But that dream was shattered for a group of AngloGold Ashanti employees who were told by a consulting company, New Horison admin, that they were short changed and should be getting more. Lloyd: I felt like I've been underpaid. That is why I ended up going to New Horisons. They said the mines are not paying people what is due to them. VO: Zwelibanzi Yende was sold a similar story by New Horison Admin.// BEAT// Formed in 2016, it's a family business run by the McPhersons in Vanderbijlpark, Gauteng. Mom Albertha, resigned as a director in 2017, but still works there. Daughter Zenobia is now the sole director and her sister Juritha handles the front desk. They claim that New Horison can retrieve extra money for their clients by reassessing and recalculating their voluntary severance packages or VSPs, including pension and provident funds as well as other benefits, such as workplace injury claims, even after they've been settled. Lloyd: For instance, on VSP, they had their own calculation. They said I've been robbed. VO: According to Lloyd Tsotetsi, it was Albertha, who in 2017 told him he should have received over a million rand more just on his VSP. He had to pay an upfront deposit of R55 000, and New Horison would take 25% of any additional funds retrieved. Lloyd: She promised that I'm gonna get it from six to eight weeks. VO: Zwelibanzi Yende's deposit was almost R79 000. New Horison recalculated his VSP and pension and told him to expect over R2.6 million extra - written on this post-it note. [beat] As far as they both understood, New Horison's 25% was based on additional funds. But Lloyd was in for a shock after his original pension settlement of around R660 000, came into his bank account. Lloyd: Then after getting my pension fund, she demanded 288,000. Derek: Did you pay that? Lloyd: She was intimidating that she'll send the Sheriff to take everything that I have. VO: He was confused - Albertha was asking for money, even though the additional 1.7 million rand he was promised on his pension was not yet forthcoming. To date he has paid New Horison over R340 000 rand, and collectively just this group of ex AngloGold Ashanti employees have forked out close to 3 million rand in fees. Four years later, they say no extra money has materialised. Maria: That lady, she must pay us back. That money doesn't belong to her, it's our money. VO: The payment of a large deposit, with the promise of substantial rewards, are the hallmarks of what the FBI calls an Advance Fee Scheme. We sent in an undercover operative to New Horison Admin to investigate, posing as a retrenched mine worker. She pays R600 for a consultation, and Juritha explains how they get their clients more money. Juritha: this is how the VSP retrenchment package works, once we get the calculations we get the upfront deposit. The upfront deposit goes with the calculations to the mine, the mine has 6 weeks to accept. If the mine does not accept in the 6 weeks, then our lawyers take over, then they take them to court, forcing them to get a court interdict to order them to pay that money. VO: So what did Juritha just say? // Freeze on shot// Labour Law expert Patrick Deale considers this sale’s spiel. Patrick: I think we have a case of fraud on our hands more commonly known as a scam - there's no basis for any of those things. They're trying to sound like big, threatening lawyers and trying to intimidate these institutions, which they have no right to, and there's no prospect of them getting anything out of them. VO: At reception, Juritha tells our undercover operative that she was short paid, despite the very scant information she was given. Juritha: So it’s 11 years and you only received under R50000… Basic salary with the 8.3 and 3.7 that you received, just a rough estimation she was at least supposed to get 300,000 VO: Amidst some light hearted banter she is handed a bundle of documents to sign Juritha: Mama, usigna full signature like you are signing at the bank. Zweli: "sign here, sign here" you see, we just sign. when I asked why can't you explain or give us these papers. so that I can take them at home to read this thing. "no, no, no, no, look, this paperwork is money, to print all those papers, you see? VO: Zenobia spins our operative a different story Zenobia: Unfortunately I do not give copies of my documentation due to the fact that fraud has been committed with it. VO: Zwelibanzi was allowed to leave with his post-it note - a record of the money he should expect. Derek: How would New Horison have arrived at these increased amounts? Patrick: There's no indication about how they came about the formula for these calculations, so they would have to explain where the right comes from and that right could only have come from their pre-existing retrenchment agreements, which, in this case, was facilitated by the CCMA. VO: After 34 years working his way up to shift boss, Itumeleng Tsuduba was also retrenched from AngloGold Ashanti and received over 2 million rand. He felt he’d got a raw deal. Itumeleng: Yeah, I was not happy. VO: His wife Elizabeth, heard about New Horison from a friend. Elizabeth: I regret that day really, because I'm the one who introduced my husband into this mess. Derek: Elizabeth, describe that meeting with Alberta. What did she promise? Elizabeth: She came up with the huge number of money pension fund is how much, retrenchment is how much, the silicosis is going to be how much, all in all, it was 11 million. Derek: You must have both felt like you'd hit the jackpot. Elizabeth: Of course yes. VO: Itumeleng ended up paying New Horison over R650 000. Derek: And you've never got a cent out of them? Elizabeth: Nothing. Even a single cent. Patrick: If you're going to tempt people, don't hang a small sweet in front of them, hang something large, that it's worth investing trust in and to induce them to pay the deposit. VO: The people who approached Carte Blanche, report that as money from their original payouts came into their bank accounts, uncannily, Albertha or Zenobia would call them demanding the 25% fee, but when they asked for their money in return they were given a slew of excuses. Zweli: So that six to eight weeks passed. So we keep on phoning them. "No, don't worry, the case is in Supreme Court. No the mine also give us problem they don't want to pay."every time stories, stories, stories. Lloyd: The last time when we went to them, the lady told us the monies are there, but Tito Mboweni is still talking to Ramaphosa to release money together with Reserve Bank. Derek: Is this the story they told you? Lloyd: Ey, big story like ay Elizabeth: When we go there she just shouting, talking vulgar language, she gonna sue us and she gonna sell our houses. Patrick: That's part of the threatening, kind of psychology to put fear into them that if they challenge it in any way, they could be in trouble. VO: And to make matters worse Zwelibanzi Yende received an additional bill for R145 000 rand. Derek: What do they say that's for? Zweli: They say for their services. telephone, Follow up. Patrick: The deposit is there as part payment of a service to be rendered. Those monies have not been received,And on that basis, the individual can cancel the contract and repay, claim repayment of the deposit for the service that has not been rendered. LINK: A group of the retrenched workers got tired of waiting and laid charges with the police in July last year. But in May they got an SMS saying that the case had been withdrawn and the docket closed VO: They called WO Pretorius for an explanation on the prosecutor's findings. Pretorius: They [New Horison Admin]) state they didn’t take anybody’s money, they took a deposit and they took money when the payouts are made into people’s accounts and the people are supposed to pay them. VO: Dissatisfied with the extent of the police investigation, the miners went back to New Horison and were met by an angry Zenobia. Sound up: Undercover day 3: Zenobia: You all know you went to the police station, mos, ne? Yes, now what do you want me to do? Zweli: I want my money back: Zenobia: I want my services, my fees for services rendered. I want that VO: And we bet she does, because according to the documents we glimpsed, their clients actually sign away 25% of any incoming benefits into their bank accounts, from the date of signature, to New Horison. The same documents they never get a copy of. VO: So the time had come for a face to face with the head honcho. Cut to Derek knocking on the door and then making the phone call… Derek: Good morning Zenobia how are you doing? It's Derek Watts from Carte Blanche. I want to speak to you about new horizon and the deposits that you've taken allegedly under false pretenses. zenobia: Derek, well you have to make an appointment. Derek: I'm right at your door. zenobia: I'm not at the office as yet. Send your queries through to me and I'll have my legal team look at it and then we can see from there VO: First they offered to go through each file in detail, //but three weeks later, they were not prepared to answer to specifics. In their response they implied that it is commonplace for companies and pension funds to “inaccurately calculate employment benefits and compensation”. Page 5 clause 15: ROR reference "The service provider has extensive knowledge and experience, that were accumulated over the past thirty years. Employers and/or administrators of the various Funds referred to, inaccurately calculates employment benefits and compensation " LINK: AngloGold Ashanti say that all of the retrenched workers were paid according to the laws and agreed by the unions. They say that they've never been approached by New Horison or any of their representatives regarding the settlements. VO: We asked New Horison to show proof of work and which institutions they had contacted, no specific proof was provided. They denied any wrongdoing and said they fulfilled their contracts with their customers. The unions for the mineworkers NUM and UASA, and pension fund Sentinel, also confirm that they have not received any disputes concerning these matters. New Horison further denies any allegation that their clients received no money, pointing to our own summary that “substantial amounts were received" and attribute those results to services they rendered. But the amounts we reflected in our summary were from the original AngloGold Ashanti settlements. Page 8 clause 25: ROR reference "The allegations that clients have not received a single cent is untrue and it is evident on your own summary that substantial amounts were received by clients respectively. It should be mentioned that the Complainants had received payments of benefits from their previous or former employers. The services the service provider rendered, resulted into payment of the correct calculation of unpaid benefits and of compensation still payable. " VO: It appears this is how New Horison understands the catch-all clause in their Client Fee Agreement, which claims 25% of all benefits received after the initial R600 consultation. Page 14 Clause 6: ROR reference "The Principal/Client shall pay the Service Provider and non-refundable consultation fee of R600.00 at the time of the initial consultation. Thereafter, the Principal/Client shall be liable to the Service Provider for Payment of the Services Provide, the fees to be equal but not to excess of 25% of the amount received. Such benefits shall include any and all payments received in terms of the Principal/Client's Employee Benefits." VO: They claim that the formula for their recalculations is privileged… and a lengthy and complicated process performed by actuaries. VO: Our undercover footage suggests otherwise Juritha: I can send it through now to the forensic auditor so that we can see how much is her VSP outstanding Undercover: Like now… Juritha: We gonna get it now Page 7 clause 21: ROR reference "Your request to disclose the "formula" of how the service provider calculates the underpaid or unpaid benefits to clients, is privileged." VO: The miners allege they were given calculations within a day of engaging their services and that recovery of funds would take 6 to 8 weeks. New Horison refutes this as not only untrue, but potentially impossible: Page 8 clause 25: ROR reference "The allegations that outstanding monies will be retrieved and/or recovered within a period of six to eight weeks, not only is untrue, but potentially impossible." [undercover] Juritha: The VSP that one there’s a upfront payment that needs to be paid, and that one takes 6-8 weeks. Page 5 clause 17: ROR reference "For purposes of the recalculation and for various types of packages, due to the complex nature of the recalculation, the service provider utilizes the services of Actuaries and legal experts to render the required services to the clients." VO: They say the ex-miners’ allegations are a smear campaign and that they're the authors of their own misfortune. Page 2 clause 4: I’m using pg 10 point 26.6 "It is abundantly clear, that the complainants that approached you, have one objection of consideration, is to drive a smearing campaign against our clients." VO: They also state "as a result of the Complainants actions, the service provider voluntarily terminated their services”, which they say could explain why payments have not been received by clients to date. And instead they claim that money is owed to them. Counter claim mentioned at Page 1 Clause 3 Page 7 clause 22: ROR reference "The service provider is not of the intention to engage into any further elaboration of the matters of those complainants that approached you, included in your list. It is however pointed out, that as a result of the Complainants actions, the service provider voluntarily terminated their services, as a result of a breakdown in the trust relationship." Patrick: These are mine workers. Can you imagine the kind of work that they've done on the mines, they finally been paid out,, and they get tempted to a pot at the end of the rainbow, and they're left destitute. Derek: So what is your hope for your financial future? Lloyd: It’s bleek. It’s doom. that pension fund that I work for 21 years is gone. Elizabeth: My husband now I can see is now no longer my husband because the few money that we did left with, we use it because we know there is huge money that is coming you can think of 11 million when its coming it’s a lot.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): No horizons for ex-miners who have had their retrenchment payments taken off them by a financial company claiming they can get them more. We confront New Horizon on their theft of ex-miners’ pension
metadata.Unique Selling Point: No Horizons – New Horison Stealing Pensions... Getting retrenched is devastating, but many are consoled by the opportunity that comes with receiving their severance package. It’s a chance to build that dream house, to pay for children and grandchildren to go to university, or to tend to medical needs for the foreseeable future. But that dream was shattered for a group of Anglo Ashanti Miners in Fochville by a company based in Vanderbijlpark, called New Horizon Administration, who has targeted ex-miners retrenchment funds for fraud. Now, most of them are facing an uncertain future.
metadata.Summary: In 2017 a group of miners took voluntary retrenchment packages offered by Anglo Ashanti Gold In Carltonville. The miners were then approached by a company based in Vanderbijlpark called New Horizon Administration run by the MacPherson family. The owner is Alberta MacPherson, managed by daughter Zenobia MacPherson - she is listed as the active director. which alleged that Anglo Ashanti had short changed the workers and that they were due more- some were promised packages to the tune of 2 Million rands each (depending on years of service), The company promised the miners that they could recover these monies from Anglo Ashanti for them( Including recalculating and getting UIF settlements for them) ... all they needed was a sizeable deposit from each miner-unfortunately many obliged and made deposits to this company. They were told they were going to get their “residual “ payments in 6 to 8 weeks... this never occurred. Anglo Ashanti has since denied ever having dealings with this company, and has stated all due monies were paid over. The company to date is still stringing the miners along.
